gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, at the price paid on the maker's store on 2026-11-17, a kit with 400 W of panels under $2,000 costs about $0.47–0.54 per Wh: ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 + 400 W at $0.48/Wh ships now, R3500 + 400 W at $0.42–0.50/Wh ships now, and BLUETTI Elite 400 + 2×200 W at $0.47/Wh ships mid-December. The four kits ChatGPT showed cost $0.61–0.81/Wh.
standout_why: StormWatts (cited, prices checked Nov 8) already uses the same method: kit price ÷ Wh, plus sun-hours from the included panels. But its 24 rows have no ALLPOWERS kit and no BLUETTI Elite 300 or Elite 400 kit. Its cheapest kit under $2,000 with about 400 W of panels is the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max + 2×220 W at $0.698/Wh. WeAreSalt (Oct 13) gives no prices, so it has no cost per Wh. It does list Wh per lb for the Elite 200 V2 (38.8) and the Jackery 2000 v2 (30.6). Solargenreview returned HTTP 429, and our own dealectric.com page failed on its TLS certificate, so I could not check either one. Some of this is already known: StormWatts lists the Jackery 2000 v2 + 2×200 W at $1,649, so ChatGPT's '$1,239 for the 400 W bundle' is already contradicted there.
decides: It changes the pick. If the measure is energy per dollar, the cheapest kits under $2,000 that ship now are ALLPOWERS kits (R2500 V2 + SP037 or R3500 + SP037), not the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 2×200 W that ChatGPT picked. That kit is a pre-order dispatching Nov 26 and costs $0.69/Wh at our link price. For a shopper who can wait, the BLUETTI Elite 400 + 2×200 W (our link, $0.47/Wh, mid-December) or the Elite 300 + 2×200 W (our link, $0.54/Wh, late November) gives 3.0–3.8 kWh under $2,000. Two caveats: with only 400 W of panels, the 3 kWh+ kits need 7.5–9.6 hours of full sun at rated output to refill. And ALLPOWERS describes the SP037 as polycrystalline, so it delivers less than its rating.
